questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How digital tech helps blind people
Famous blind artists and writers in history
How guide dogs are trained
Why smartphones are bad for our eyes
questions.why: They look at inventions, like smartphone apps, that dramatically improve blind people's lives.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention Homer, Ray Charles and Jorge Borges?
options: They all invented something for blind people
They all lived in the same country
They were all musicians
They were all blind but were great artists
questions.why: Neil says they were all blind, and Georgina says it didn't hold them back.

questions.q: Which of these can the 'BeMyEyes' app help blind users do?
options: Read printed books and newspapers aloud to them
Find lost keys and match the colours of their clothes
Drive a car safely on busy roads in the city
Replace their white cane completely when walking
questions.why: Apps like BeMyEyes let users find lost keys, cross busy roads and colour match clothes.

questions.q: What is Brian Mwenda's device designed to do?
options: Replace the white cane with a smart phone app
Read text from a phone screen out loud to the user
Clip onto a white cane and detect obstacles ahead
Guide users around the city with a talking map
questions.why: He says once you clip it onto any white cane it works to detect obstacles in front of you.

questions.q: How does the 'Sixth Sense' device work?
options: It sends out sound and measures the echoes, like bats
It uses a small camera and GPS to find the way home
It vibrates when a friend or family member is near
It uses a beam of light to scan the road ahead
questions.why: It uses echo-location: a sound pulse bounces off an obstacle to show how far away it is.

questions.q: What does Georgina think being able to move around confidently does for blind people?
options: It makes them rely more on others
It makes their phones more expensive
It really increases their independence
It helps them see better
questions.why: Georgina says being able to move around confidently really boosts people's independence.

questions.q: What does Fern Lulham hope will happen as society sees more blind people in everyday life?
options: More apps will be invented for them
Blind people will stop using apps
People will feel sorry for them
Disability will seem more normal
questions.why: She says it helps tackle stereotypes and 'just normalises disability'.

questions.q: Why does Neil ask listeners to close their eyes and move around the room?
options: To test how well they can hear sounds
To show how useful the technology is
To practise using a white cane
To help them relax
questions.why: He says you'll see how difficult it is and how life changing this technology can be.
